Subject: Hosted API pricing — commit tiers & security gating?

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency profile. Before we can move to an internal approval, procurement/legal have two gating questions: 1) Does Veridian need to provide SOC2 evidence (Type II) and an executed DPA before we can lock in commit pricing (per-token rebates)? 2) How do commit tiers map to monthly invoices if our usage spikes above the committed level?

High level ask: we’re evaluating a 12-month usage commit (estimate ~6B tokens/month) and need to understand any compliance pre-conditions and the cadence for applying the per-token rebate. Can you share a sample DPA and the SOC2 artifacts you can provide?

Thanks,
Anna McCoy

Veridian Health
Anna.McCoy@veridian-health.com

Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — commit tiers & security gating?

Hi Anna — great to hear the demo landed well. Short answers up front:

- Yes, for commit-tier pricing we require an executed DPA (standard) and SOC2 Type II evidence to enable enterprise pricing. The SOC2 may be delivered as a redacted report or SOC2 summary; we can also provide a security attestation letter for procurement if you need a faster handoff.

- Rebates are applied retroactively on a monthly basis: you are invoiced at list (or discounted committed) rate, and if your monthly usage exceeds the committed threshold for that tier we apply the higher-tier per-token rebate for the entire month (we can also do prorated banded tiers on request). For spikes above commitment we support burst pricing — those tokens are billed at the next-tier list rate unless you choose a buffer band.

I've attached a redacted SOC2 Type II summary and our standard DPA (Draft_DPA_Veridian_v3.docx). A typical timeline we see: 1–2 weeks for procurement review, 2–4 weeks for legal to review the DPA, and security/infosec will typically validate the SOC2 evidence within 7–10 business days. We typically make the commit pricing effective upon execution of the DPA and delivery of SOC2 evidence (or an agreed alternative attestation).

If it helps, we can:
- Provide a redacted SOC2 today (attached)
- Offer a 30-day provisional pricing hold for budgeting while legal reviews the DPA (pricing finalizes when DPA executed)
- Add a contract clause that credits any difference retroactively if evidence is delivered within X days after signing — happy to scope that with you.

Next steps: can you confirm procurement’s preferred review timeline and whether they need the full SOC2 PDF or a redacted summary? I’ll also loop in our legal lead (Marissa) to speed DPA comments.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Americas
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — commit tiers & security gating? (math + clause suggestion)

Hi Anna — quick follow on the economics and a proposed contract language to avoid ambiguity.

Pricing mechanics (example):
- Proposed tier: 6B tokens/month commit -> committed per-token = $0.0008
- Band above commit: 6B–8B -> per-token rebate steps to $0.00075 (banded)
- Burst beyond 8B -> billed at on-demand list $0.0010 for overflow

We apply rebate as a true-up on the monthly invoice once usage is finalized. If you prefer, we can instead apply tiered rebates only to tokens within each band (tiered billing) — that’s configurable in the SOW.

Suggested clause for the SOW: "Commit pricing shall become effective upon execution of the Data Processing Agreement and receipt by Redwood of SOC2 Type II evidence (redacted or full report acceptable). If Customer executes the SOW prior to delivery of SOC2 evidence, Customer shall be eligible for provisional pricing for a period of 30 days pending submission; full commit rebates will be applied retroactively upon delivery and validation of SOC2 evidence, subject to Redwood’s standard security verification."

If legal needs a harder guarantee, we can offer an escrow-like instrument where a portion of the first month’s commitment is held as credits until SOC2 is validated; we’ve done that for a couple of large health customers.

Let me know whether Veridian prefers banded true-up or whole-month uplift and I’ll update the numbers in the draft SOW.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Principal, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Thanks Stephanie and Marcus — this is helpful. Procurement confirms they need either the full SOC2 Type II or a redacted report plus an attestation letter; legal will review the draft DPA and expects comments within 5–7 business days.

We prefer the banded true-up (tokens billed per band) and the proposed clause is acceptable to start. For the escrow approach, procurement would need the details in writing (amount held, release conditions).

Next steps for us:
- Veridian legal to review Draft_DPA_Veridian_v3.docx (cc’d)
- Veridian procurement to confirm PO template and internal sign-off timeline
- Please send a DocuSign-ready version of the SOW + DPA when you have redlines incorporated.

Can you put the DocuSign link in your next reply and confirm who on Redwood will be the signing authority? We’d like to have the SOC2 validated and the DPA executed before finance issues the first monthly invoice.

Appreciate the flexibility — looking forward to closing this.
